result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.pagerank()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate PageRank scores for all nodes in the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L13915-L14053){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.pagerank( damping=0.85, max_iter=100, tol=1e-06, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Rank propagation](/assets/graphs/algo-rank-propagation.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A source node on the left in the accent color, with four directed accent-colored arrows fanning out to four downstream neighbors on the right, illustrating how a node's rank is distributed to its out-neighbors each iteration." width="100%"} PageRank is a link analysis algorithm that assigns importance scores to nodes based on their incoming connections. Originally developed by Google to rank web pages, it's widely used in social network analysis, recommendation systems, and influence detection. The algorithm iteratively distributes "rank" from each node to its neighbors, with a damping factor to model random jumps. Nodes with many incoming edges from high-ranking nodes receive higher scores. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [damping]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.85]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The probability of following an edge (vs. random jump). Higher values (closer to `1.0`) give more weight to the graph structure. Typical range: `0.8`-`0.95`. [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of iterations to run. The algorithm stops early if convergence is reached. [tol]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1e-06]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Convergence tolerance. The algorithm stops when the sum of absolute differences between iterations is less than this value. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Column name to store PageRank scores in the node DataFrame. If `None` (default), automatically uses `pagerank`. Overwrites column if it already exists. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores in NDF and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to PageRank scores (sum to `1.0`). If `return_dict` is `False` (default): returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Since "Charlie" receives incoming links from both "Alice" and "Bob", it accumulates more rank than either of them: ::: {#a045e655 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="Alice") .add_node(label="Bob") .add_node(label="Charlie") ) alice_id = graph.get_id_from_label("Alice") bob_id = graph.get_id_from_label("Bob") charlie_id = graph.get_id_from_label("Charlie") graph.add_edge(alice_id, bob_id) graph.add_edge(alice_id, charlie_id) graph.add_edge(bob_id, charlie_id) scores = graph.pagerank(return_dict=True) scores ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {1: 0.1975796492961225, 3: 0.520869350456903, 2: 0.28155100024697455} ``` ::: ::: Node IDs can be mapped back to labels for a more readable result: ::: {#0142aa68 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} {graph.get_label_from_id(nid): score for nid, score in scores.items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {'Alice': 0.1975796492961225, 'Charlie': 0.520869350456903, 'Bob': 0.28155100024697455} ``` ::: ::: Lowering `damping=` increases the influence of random jumps relative to the graph structure, which tends to pull every node's score closer together: ::: {#5849d8d1 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="Alice") .add_node(label="Bob") .add_node(label="Charlie") ) graph.add_edge(source="Alice", target="Bob") graph.add_edge(source="Alice", target="Charlie") graph.add_edge(source="Bob", target="Charlie") graph.pagerank(damping=0.5, return_dict=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {1: 0.24242424242424246, 3: 0.45454545454545464, 2: 0.30303030303030304} ``` ::: ::: Sorting the results surfaces the most influential nodes first: ::: {#de33bff4 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="Alice") .add_node(label="Bob") .add_node(label="Charlie") ) graph.add_edge(source="Alice", target="Bob") graph.add_edge(source="Alice", target="Charlie") graph.add_edge(source="Bob", target="Charlie") scores = graph.pagerank(return_dict=True) sorted( ((graph.get_label_from_id(nid), score) for nid, score in scores.items()), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True, ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` [('Charlie', 0.520869350456903), ('Bob', 0.28155100024697455), ('Alice', 0.1975796492961225)] ``` ::: :::
